gloss: to step forward; to take the first step

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {踏|ふ}み{出|だ}しませんでした

definitions.gloss: to step forward; to step out
definitions.explanation: To physically move a foot forward or step outside a boundary.

definitions.gloss: to take the first step; to embark on
definitions.explanation: To begin a new endeavor or venture, often overcoming hesitation. A figurative extension of the physical meaning.

examples.japanese: {一歩|いっぽ}{前|まえ}に{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}す。
{白線|はくせん}から{足|あし}を{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}さないでください。
examples.english: Please do not step past the white line.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はステージに{向|む}かって{力強|ちからづよ}く{一歩|いっぽ}を{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}した。
examples.english: She took a strong step toward the stage.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{世界|せかい}へ{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To step into a new world.

examples.japanese: {勇気|ゆうき}を{出|だ}して{最初|さいしょ}の{一歩|いっぽ}を{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I gathered my courage and took the first step.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{夢|ゆめ}だった{独立|どくりつ}に{向|む}けて、ついに{一歩|いっぽ}を{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}すことにした。
examples.english: I finally decided to take the first step toward my long-held dream of going independent.

notes:
{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}す is a transitive godan verb. Compound of {踏|ふ}む (to step on) + {出|だ}す (to put out). Sense 2 is very common in motivational and life-change contexts.

ASPECT (ている):
Rarely used in the ている form since it describes a momentary action.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一歩|いっぽ}を{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}す (take a step)
- ～へ{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}す (step out toward)
- ～から{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}す (step out from)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一歩|いっぽ}を{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}す (take the first step)
- {最初|さいしょ}の{一歩|いっぽ}を{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}す (take the very first step)
- {新|あたら}しい{一歩|いっぽ}を{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}す (take a new step forward)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {踏|ふ}み{込|こ}む: to step into, to tread into (entering a place or situation more deeply)
- {乗|の}り{出|だ}す: to set out, to embark (emphasizes beginning an active venture)
